correctness.rationale: Integrating the exact periodic equation gives the cubic moment identity because the autocorrelation has mean equal to the square of the mean of \(\gamma\). Fourier transformation gives \(\widehat C(k)=|\widehat\gamma(k)|^2\). If a nonconstant solution had maximal positive Fourier mode \(m\), the covariance side would have no \(3m\)-mode while the cubic term would contribute exactly \(\widehat\gamma(m)^3\neq0\). The constant case is excluded by \(\gamma(0)=1\). The theorem is conditional and makes no existence or convergence claim.
